I never went to school, so I don't read much. My husband and me, we got these 4 mu of land in the village, and he works at a factory in town when there's no urgent work on the farm. That means most days I'm alone in the fields. I've been farming since I was little — my mother and my mother-in-law taught me everything I know. We don't have much cash, so I have to be careful. Last year I bought too much fertilizer for the wheat and then we were short when it came time to buy the maize seed. This year I'm going to be more careful.

**Winter wheat**

I plant wheat around October 10th, same as everyone here. I save some seed from last year — maybe two-thirds — and buy a little new seed from the shop so it doesn't get weak. I spread about half a bag of that white compound fertilizer on the ground before planting, then I go over it with the small tiller my brother-in-law lent us. That's the base. In the spring, around Qingming, I look at the wheat. If it's yellowish, I topdress with urea. Last year I put down too much, so this year I'll do a bit less — maybe one big scoop per mu at jointing instead of two. I irrigate three times: once right after planting if the soil is dry, once when it greens up in March, and once at jointing. The well water costs money to pump, but without it the wheat won't fill. I don't use pesticide on wheat — we never have, and I don't want to spend that money.

**Summer maize**

As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, we plant the maize. My husband takes a day off to help because we have to do it fast — usually by hand with a hoe, since the tractor drivers don't like coming for just 4 mu. I buy hybrid seed from the shop, the yellow bags everyone buys, about 3 jin per mu. When I plant, I put a handful of fertilizer in each hole — that's the only time I fertilize the maize. If it rains good in July and August, I might only irrigate once, at the big trumpet leaf stage. If it's dry, maybe twice. I don't hire much labor — maybe one person for one day to help harvest the wheat if my husband can't get off work. Mostly it's just us.

I'm hoping for about 380 jin per mu of wheat and maybe 420 jin per mu of maize. If we get that, we'll have enough to eat and sell a little, plus money for seed next year. I wanted to put more fertilizer, but we just don't have the cash right now, and I'd rather have money in hand for if someone gets sick.
